question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Official policy momentum toward a 10-year baseline under Earned Settlement is strong, with government proposals and a public consultation open through early 2026.
Implementation timing signals target 2026, potentially around April, which elevates near-term likelihood of a 10-year baseline by May 2026.
There are non-trivial risks of delay from parliamentary calendars, ministerial changes, legal challenges, and transitional carve-outs that could push the effective date beyond May 2026.
Forecasts and third-party analyses (e.g., Metaculus around 55%, Commons Library briefings) indicate substantial uncertainty and provide credible downside risk to immediate adoption.

justification.critique_assessment: The objections identify credible bottlenecks in legislation, implementation, and timing; they reveal genuine risk of delay that justifies trimming from the ensemble.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted from 0.87 to 0.75 to reflect downside risk from parliamentary delays, legal challenges, and the open consultation window, while preserving momentum signals.

forecasts.reference-class: Forecasts on UK immigration policy reform to the settlement path (earned settlement) with a baseline 10-year qualifying period, policy details and timing anchored to 2025–2026 consultations and proposals

sources.claim: Forecast on whether the UK will increase the settlement qualifying period to 10 years before May 2026; currently 55% chance.
Government consultation on earned settlement proposes raising the baseline qualifying period to 10 years (with exceptions) and indicates the period will be subject to the consultation outcome.

House of Commons Library briefing notes that the November 2025 government announcement would set a baseline 10-year period for settlement, with exemptions; implementation could occur in 2026 following the consultation.
Migration Observatory analysis describing proposed changes (10-year baseline, penalties for public funds, consultation open until Feb 2026) and that outcomes depend on the consultation.

Migration Advisory Committee 2025 report notes current ILR can be reached around year 5, while the policy direction (earned settlement with a 10-year baseline) is being considered in the 2025–2026 policy process.
The government proposes increasing the standard qualifying period for settlement to 10 years, with exceptions, and opened a public consultation that runs into February 2026.
House of Commons Library summary states baseline 10-year settlement for most migrants announced in 2025, with consultation open until 12 February 2026.
Migration Observatory notes the 5-to-10 year increase with carve-outs and mentions the public consultation window ending February 2026.
Accessible version states the default qualifying period for settlement would be increased to 10 years, with potential for shorter paths via “earned settlement.”
Official Earned Settlement consultation page announces a 10-year baseline for settlement and notes policy details will be finalized after consultation.
House of Commons Library briefing summarises the 10-year baseline proposal and indicates changes depend on the consultation results.
Parliamentary record outlines the shift to a 10-year baseline for settlement and that the policy is subject to public consultation.
Legal update notes the 12-week consultation (closing Feb 12, 2026) and indicates implementation could begin from April 2026.
September 2025 government announcement describing a contribution-based settlement framework with a 10-year baseline as the default.
